linkedin: I’m building FliperOS, a free and open-source Linux distribution (Ubuntu 24.04) that turns a PC into an arcade cabinet for CRT monitors. Version {version} is out.
What it solves: playing arcade games on a real 15 kHz tube normally means hours of kernel patches, modelines and emulator configs. FliperOS ships all of it ready:
• a Linux 6.18 kernel with the 15 kHz patches and Switchres, so AMD cards output a true 240p signal (Intel and NVIDIA work too, with super resolutions)
• GroovyMAME, RetroArch, Flycast, Dolphin, PCSX2, Keisho (Model 2/3) and more, each started with the right video mode
• a setup menu drawn for the tube itself, and a web panel to control the cabinet from a phone: pick a game, watch it live, put the screen in OBS
• party play between linked cabinets over the local network
Latest: Odin (Sega Hikaru and Gaelco 3D) and HBMAME with Switchres, both installed on demand the first time you open one of their games.
It ships no games and no BIOS. Source, releases and docs are open, and feedback and contributions are welcome: {url}
